The '''Coronado knight''' is a member of the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel]] in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]]. He appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{In|FOTV|noin}}.

==Background==
Nothing is known about his history other than his status as a [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Knights|knight]] of the Coronado chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] by 2296. He later accompanied his chapter after the [[Coronado elder|elder]] received an invitation to a meeting being held by the [[Knights of San Fernando]] along with the [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]] and [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite]] chapters that year.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Golden Rule]]===
The knight arrives with the rest of his chapter aboard their [[Brotherhood airship|airship]] to the San Fernando chapter's newly acquired headquarters, [[Area 51]]. He stands in rank during the meeting of elders, witnessing their unanimous decision to rebel against the dominant [[Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel|Commonwealth chapter]] to shift power within the wider Brotherhood back to the West Coast.

During subsequent celebrations, as [[Maximus]] is trying to walk away while a pair of [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60]]-outfitted knights duel each other for sport, the muscly Coronado knight aggressively confronts him, asking if he was the one who took down the "[[New California Republic|NCR]] bitch" [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] (whom he refers to as "Mold Over"). Once Maximus confirms it, the knight demands they have a fight; he rebukes Maximus' attempt to get his armor by stating they will be fighting "bare-back:" no [[power armor]] and with their strength and skill alone.

The fight initially goes in the knight's favor due to his stronger physique and taking a cheap shot as Maximus was removing his jacket. His enemy's advantage forces Maximus to use his cunning instead, landing a punch to the knight's crotch, then stunning him by throwing his jacket in the man's face, allowing him to land some hits himself. The knight decides to increase the threat level by bringing out a [[Combat knife (TV series)|combat knife]], forcing Maximus to dodge his attacks until he is able to force the knight to the ground after maneuvering him to disembowel himself. Maximus eventually overpowers his enemy and sinks the blade into his chest, killing him. The knight is left lying on the floor when [[Xander Harkness]] flies into the hangar in his [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibird]]. Harkness briefly expresses confusion when he notices the fight and then silently commends Maximus for his victory.<ref>{{FOTV|2|2}}</ref>

==Personality==
The knight is shown to be brash and impulsive, deliberately seeking out the physically weaker Maximus to try and confirm that he really was worthy of his fame as Moldaver's killer, then challenging him to a physical fight to assess if he lives up to his reputation in person. He is also shown to be willing to use dirty tactics to win a fight such as striking Maximus while he was removing his jacket and couldn't use his arms, and pulling out his combat knife once he was on the losing end despite being the one to demand the fight in the first place.
